logline: A hotel heir tangled in an inheritance war and a perpetually smiling employee collide in a luxury hospitality empire where charm is currency and every smile hides a cost.

renewal.note: Completed its 16-episode run on JTBC and Netflix in August 2023. No sequel or continuation announced.

bollymeter.basis: Sizzling lead chemistry from Lee Jun-ho and Im Yoon-ah keeps the show afloat, but a thin script and formulaic conflict arcs dragged the 75% RT score with only 8 critic reviews - a muted endorsement for a romance that coasts on star power.

pull_quotes.text: The show fully embraces the humour in the well-trodden path as the main love story unfolds.

seasons.review_body: King the Land premiered on JTBC in June 2023 and landed on Netflix globally the same day, riding considerable anticipation built around its two leads: 2PM singer-actor Lee Jun-ho and Girls' Generation's Im Yoon-ah. The chemistry delivers on paper - the luxury hotel setting is lush, the will-they-won't-they push-pull is professionally executed, and Lee Jun-ho's grand prize trot at the 2023 Asia Artist Awards confirmed audience affection for his performance. The problem is structural: at 16 episodes the show repeats its central misunderstanding arc far past its tension point, and the antagonists belong to a K-drama template circa 2015. The Rotten Tomatoes tally of 75% from just 8 critics reflects the show's watchability without endorsing its ambition. A solid date-night drama; a forgettable one the week after.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A stylish premiere that establishes the hotel empire backdrop and drops the two leads into each other's orbit with precise comic timing.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sa-rang's reflexively professional smile in the face of Gu Won's open disdain - the show's thesis in a single expression.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A tidy finale that resolves its threads without surprising anyone - closure over catharsis, but the leads sell it.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final reconciliation scene in the hotel lobby, shot with the same visual grammar as the opening meeting.
